models.summary: A Bertalanffy rate, closed as a Chapman-Richards curve, then thinned because a harvested stand is less dense than a virgin one. The rate is synthesis minus destruction, both powers of the carbon already stored. The seed carbon is set to zero. The closed form is a cap times one minus an exponential, raised to a third coordinate. Harvested-stand carbon multiplies that form by the mean life over the harvest age. The print splits that ratio across two lines. Products are sawn wood, panels, and paper, with recovery rates 30, 10, and 70 percent and lives 35, 25, and 2 years. The paper states the weighted product factor as 8.674 years. The product shares that would produce 8.674 are drawn and not printed. Total carbon is the thinned stand times one plus that factor over the harvest age. The introducing sentence swaps the names of the stand part and the product part. A later revision mixes a harvested share and an uncut share, then the paper sets the revision aside except for one case. Tropical and temperate carbon peak at 59.90 years, at 790.4 and 634.9 tons per hectare. Frigid carbon peaks at 63.45 years, at 314.0.
models.computational_cost: A closed curve evaluated over harvest age, once per climate
models.purpose: Turn a harvest age into stand carbon plus product carbon.
objectives: Maximize carbon per hectare over the harvest age.

models.summary: Three indices, two pies, and a rule that a curve with no peak means no cut. Carbon is the total store divided by 274.1 tons per hectare, the stated average of primary forests, and the store itself is a mix of the harvested share and the uncut share. The economical index multiplies the harvest rate by a sigmoid of age and a growth term. The print does not parse. Biodiversity subtracts a harvest penalty. The print places one plus an exponential of age over mean life above a base-2 logarithm of 2. The prose says that at age zero the index equals one minus the harvest share, which a logarithm that is zero at age zero would not give. The pies, which the sentences do not number, read 15.71, 59.36, and 24.93 for carbon, economy, and biodiversity in developing countries, and 14.29, 28.57, and 57.14 in developed countries. Both triples sum to 100. The developed triple is 1, 2, and 4 parts in 7. The summary says developed countries put more weight on carbon. The pie puts carbon last, and biodiversity first. Culture is named and then absent.

models.summary: The same three weights, applied to areas rather than to a hectare. Carbon uses the whole forest, because wetlands, lakes, and grassland also store carbon. Money uses only the wooded area, because the unwooded part yields no timber in this model. Biodiversity uses the wooded index on the wooded area and leaves the rest uncut. The second equality in that biodiversity line does not parse. The wooded share is rho. The average value is the carbon index, plus rho times the economic weight times the economical index, plus the biodiversity weight times one minus rho times one minus the biodiversity index. On the Amazon the paper states a century store of 3.702 times 10 to the 11 tons of carbon, from a stand store of 690.40 tons per hectare, a harvest age of 59.90 years, and a Brazil area of 3.212 times 10 to the 8 hectares. It calls that store carbon dioxide and labels the unit as tons of carbon.
